paperTitle: Perceptions of Voice Interaction in Digital Games: A Comparative Study
centralContribution: This study investigates and comparatively analyzes perceptions of voice interaction in digital games across three core scenarios (game-to-player, player-to-player, player-to-game) among game experts, undergraduate students, and generative AIs, aiming to provide insights for improving gameplay experiences, reducing disruptive behaviors, and identifying opportunities for health and wellness applications.

elements.name: Central Contribution of the Study
elements.description: The study's central contribution is a comparative analysis of perceptions regarding voice interaction in digital games, involving human experts, students, and generative AIs across three interaction scenarios (game-to-player, player-to-player, player-to-game). The aim is to enhance gameplay, mitigate disruptive behaviors, and explore applications in health and wellness.
elements.justification: This element directly states the core innovation and purpose of the research, making it the most critical piece of information for understanding the paper.

elements.name: Paper Abstract
elements.description: Voice interaction, despite its ubiquity in daily life, faces fluctuating integration in digital games due to technical limitations (e.g., microphone quality, transcription inaccuracies, ambient noise) and socio-behavioral issues (e.g., toxic player conduct, identity dissonance). This challenge is particularly acute in health-related games where voice interaction is scarce despite its potential for accessibility and rehabilitation. The paper addresses this by conducting a comparative study to understand diverse perceptions of voice interaction, leveraging advancements in AI and voice recognition to guide future game development, especially for enhancing immersion, engagement, and health applications.
elements.justification: This abstract provides a concise overview of the paper's context, the problem it addresses, and its general approach, which is fundamental to grasping the study's relevance.

elements.name: Comparative Likert Scale Results for Human and AI Participants
elements.description: This figure illustrates the average scores and standard deviations from a 5-point Likert scale for positively (blue) and negatively (pink) phrased questions, as answered by game experts, undergraduate students, and generative AIs.
elements.justification: This figure is central to evaluating the study's quantitative results, directly comparing the perceptions of human and AI subjects across the research questions, thus highlighting key findings and differences.

elements.name: Voice Interaction Scenarios and Questionnaire Items
elements.description: This table lists the specific questions (Q1-Q15) used in the 5-point Likert scale questionnaire, categorized under the three core voice interaction scenarios: Game interacts with the player, Player interacts with another player, and Player interacts with the game.
elements.justification: This table is crucial for understanding the methodology and the specific aspects of voice interaction that were surveyed. It provides context for interpreting the quantitative results presented in other tables and figures.
